question.problem:
Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curve $x=3-{y}^{2}$ and the line $y=1-x.$ 
Express ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/8a46756cd4842caf7977ef72ae05912a635843a06382b21136362455a94369e4.png)

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.   Notice that we're using that $x=3-{y}^{2}$ can be split into $y=\pm \sqrt{3-x}.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/43da7a61d7a4bff15274cdacbf1f3265c097edb8740583c69463460467f8100f.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 2,\,1-x\le y\le \sqrt{3-x}\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,2\le x\le 3,\,-\sqrt{3-x}\le y\le \sqrt{3-x}\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{1-x}^{\sqrt{3-x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{-\sqrt{3-x}}^{\sqrt{3-x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
